## Simple explanation

W&B is a hosted platform and set of tools that helps teams record machine
learning runs, compare metrics, and share experiment results.

## Technical explanation

The platform can log run configuration, metrics, system information, files,
and artifacts, and can group runs into projects or sweeps. Logged outputs
depend on what the training code sends to the service. Teams should understand
data retention, access controls, and whether prompts, samples, or other
sensitive data are being logged.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Experiment tracking makes iterative development more auditable and helps
identify which code, configuration, and data produced a result. It can reduce
manual spreadsheet work, but reproducibility still requires deliberate
versioning and complete run metadata.

## How it works

Initialize a run from training code, log configuration and metrics over time,
and save important artifacts such as checkpoints or evaluation outputs.
Compare runs through dashboards or programmatic APIs, and record the versions
of datasets and model code used.

## Practical example

During hyperparameter tuning, log each run's learning rate, batch size,
validation metric, and source revision. Compare candidates on the same
validation protocol, then store the final model artifact with a traceable
reference.

## Common misconceptions

- Logging a metric does not ensure the metric is computed correctly or that
  experiments are directly comparable.
- A tracking service is not a substitute for source control, data governance,
  or a production model registry.
